_comment: Single source of truth for busybox-ash bashism detection (T-bash-on-demand). Loaded at runtime by BOTH iOS (bundle resource) and Android (asset). Every rule is grounded in on-device testing against Alpine 3.21.0 / BusyBox 1.37.0 ash (tested 2026-07-18). Patterns MUST stay inside the common ICU/java.util.regex dialect subset, MUST NOT contain nested quantifiers (ReDoS), and are matched LINE BY LINE against the script with heredoc BODIES stripped. tier: S = silent-wrong under ash (highest priority, never prune), E = loud error under ash, T1 = explicit bash reference (ensure installed, do not switch interpreter).

rules.name: bash-shebang
rules.behaviorNote: Script declares a bash interpreter; without bash installed the kernel reports 'not found'.
rules.fixHint: Use `#!/bin/sh` and remove bash-only syntax, or let Minis install bash.

rules.name: bash-invoke
rules.behaviorNote: bash is invoked as a command (command-head position only; `grep bash` etc. does not match).
rules.fixHint: Invoke `sh` instead if the target script is POSIX, or let Minis install bash.

rules.name: arith-command
rules.behaviorNote: busybox sh parses (( )) as nested subshells and runs the expression as a COMMAND (exit 127); `if (( x > y ))` silently takes the WRONG branch.
rules.fixHint: Comparisons: `[ "$x" -gt 5 ]`. Arithmetic assignment: `x=$((x + 1))` ($((..)) expansion IS supported).

rules.name: compound-assign
rules.behaviorNote: busybox sh treats `x+=1` as a COMMAND named 'x+=1' ('not found'); the variable is never updated while the script appears to run.
rules.fixHint: Numeric: `x=$((x + n))`. String append: `s="${s}suffix"`. Array append: `list="$list item"` or `set -- "$@" item`.

rules.name: brace-range
rules.behaviorNote: busybox sh does not brace-expand; `{1..3}` is passed through as the LITERAL string with no error.
rules.fixHint: Write the list out (`1 2 3`) or use `$(seq 1 3)` for numeric ranges.

rules.name: printf-v
rules.behaviorNote: busybox printf has no -v; output becomes '-v ...' and the variable is never assigned, with no error.
rules.fixHint: Use command substitution: `var=$(printf 'fmt' args)`.

rules.name: array-def
rules.behaviorNote: Arrays are unsupported: `a=(1 2 3)` is a syntax error in busybox sh.
rules.fixHint: Use a space-separated string (`a="1 2 3"; for x in $a; do ...`) or positional parameters (`set -- 1 2 3`).

rules.name: array-expand
rules.behaviorNote: `${a[@]}` / `${#a[@]}` are 'bad substitution' in busybox sh.
rules.fixHint: With positional parameters use `"$@"` and `$#`; with a space-separated string iterate with `for`.

rules.name: process-subst
rules.behaviorNote: Process substitution fails at runtime: can't open '/dev/fd/NN'.
rules.fixHint: Write to temp files: `cmd1 >/tmp/f1; cmd2 >/tmp/f2; diff /tmp/f1 /tmp/f2`.

rules.name: c-for
rules.behaviorNote: C-style for loops are a syntax error ('bad for loop variable').

rules.name: case-conv
rules.behaviorNote: `${x^^}` / `${x,,}` case conversion is 'bad substitution'.
rules.fixHint: `$(echo "$x" | tr a-z A-Z)` (or `tr A-Z a-z`).

rules.name: indirect-ref
rules.behaviorNote: `${!name}` indirect expansion is 'bad substitution'.
rules.fixHint: `eval "val=\$$name"` (be careful: eval executes its argument).

rules.name: pipe-amp
rules.behaviorNote: `cmd |& next` is a syntax error.
rules.fixHint: `cmd 2>&1 | next`

rules.name: local-opt
rules.behaviorNote: `local -x v=1` fails ('bad variable name'); plain `local` works.
rules.fixHint: `local v=1; export v`

rules.name: mapfile
rules.behaviorNote: mapfile/readarray are 'not found' and downstream array use cascades.
rules.fixHint: `while IFS= read -r line; do ...; done < file`

rules.name: select-in
rules.behaviorNote: `select x in ...` menus are a syntax error.
rules.fixHint: Print a numbered list with printf and read the choice with `read`.

rules.name: extglob
rules.behaviorNote: extglob patterns like `@(a|b)` are a syntax error.
rules.fixHint: Use a `case` statement with multiple patterns, or separate globs.

rules.name: declare
rules.behaviorNote: `declare` is 'not found' AND the variable is NOT assigned (verified), so later logic sees an empty value.
rules.fixHint: Assign directly (`x=5`). Associative arrays have no sh equivalent — use `case` or key=value lines in a temp file.

rules.name: export-f
rules.behaviorNote: `export -f` is 'illegal option'.
rules.fixHint: Define the function inside the invoked script, or extract it into its own script file.

rules.name: here-string
rules.behaviorNote: Here-strings are 'syntax error: unexpected redirection'.
rules.fixHint: `printf '%s\n' "$s" | cmd` (note: the pipe runs cmd in a subshell).

rules.name: read-a
rules.behaviorNote: `read -a arr` is 'illegal option' and array use cascades.
rules.fixHint: `read v1 v2 rest` for fixed fields, or `set -- $line` for word-splitting into positional parameters.

rules.name: coproc
rules.behaviorNote: `coproc` is 'not found'.
rules.fixHint: Use a named pipe (`mkfifo`) with a background process.
